iut_type: End Product (Silex Technology module, for end customer 'P company'), TCRL2024-1 scheduled HOGP/ScPP test item additions
customer_question: Our HOGP/ScPP PTS test report was just completed by our subcontractor — can you confirm it's sufficient evidence for registration?
question_variants: Is our current HOGP/ScPP test report enough, or will it become outdated soon?
What additional test items will be required if registration is delayed past a certain date?
actual_issue: The customer's registration timeline had been pushed back (to around January, due to the end customer's product release schedule change), and needed to know whether their already-completed HOGP/ScPP test report would still be valid as evidence once that delayed registration date arrived, given upcoming scheduled test specification updates.
plain_english_explanation: Comparing the submitted HOGP/ScPP test report's Pass items against a freshly-generated Test Plan from the same ICS configuration confirmed no missing items for any registration completed by December 27, 2024. However, TCRL2024-1 was scheduled to add 10 new HOGP test items effective December 28, 2024 — meaning any registration completed on or after that date would require those 10 additional test items to be run and added as evidence, beyond what the current report already covered.
consultant_answer: Your current HOGP/ScPP report is sufficient evidence with no missing items for any registration completed by December 27, 2024. However, TCRL2024-1 adds 10 new HOGP test items effective December 28, 2024 — since your registration is now expected around January, you'll need to run and add those 10 additional items as evidence before registering.
decision_logic: Test report sufficiency should be evaluated against the specific TCRL version in effect at the actual planned registration date, not just the version in effect when testing was originally performed — a scheduled TCRL update with a known effective date can retroactively add requirements for a delayed registration timeline.
final_recommendation: When a customer's registration timeline shifts due to external factors (like an end customer's release schedule change), proactively check for any scheduled TCRL updates with effective dates falling within the new timeline, and flag any additional test items that would become required as a result.
risk_if_done_wrong: Failing to flag the TCRL2024-1 scheduled test item additions could result in the customer submitting an incomplete test report for a registration attempted after December 28, 2024, requiring a late-stage scramble to add the missing items.
